title: Allocate a valid RPL DIO Time Option type across spec and implementations
description: Correctness review finding. python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:111-167 defines DIO_TIME_OPTION_TYPE = 0 and encodes an eight-byte Type/Length option. RFC 6550 assigns RPL Control Message Option Type 0 to Pad1, whose wire form is one octet and has no Length field. python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:106-141 and test/vectors/packets-timing.json:239-244 currently canonize the colliding 00 06 prefix. A standards-compliant RPL option walker will consume 00 as Pad1 and parse 06 as the next option type, so the advertised time cannot interoperate and may desynchronize all following options. spec/09-packets-timing.md:211-223 still says Type TBD.
acceptance_criteria: Select and document a non-conflicting provisional/assigned RPL option type through the project extension allocation process, or disable wire emission until such a type is selected. Update spec/09-packets-timing.md, docs/drafts as applicable, Python, Rust, Zephyr/C, and test/vectors/packets-timing.json to one canonical allocation and layout. Add independent tests showing Type 0 is handled as RFC 6550 Pad1 without reading a length, the selected time option round-trips through a normal mixed RPL option list, unknown and malformed options are handled correctly, and every implementation consumes the same vector. Run focused cross-implementation tests and three code-review passes on each modified source module.
notes: Python/spec registry is now 0x15, but Zephyr C rpl_messages.h still defines DIO Time as 0/Pad1 and messages.c ignores reserved, permits stratum outside 0-4, permits NO_SYNC with nonzero timestamp, and lacks focused codec vectors. Update C to 0x15 with strict parse/write validation and mixed option iterator tests; validate on Linux/EC2 per project rules before closing cross-implementation scope.
